name: Meadowsweet
grown_as: A native perennial wild flower of damp meadows, ditches and riversides, also grown for its scent and pollinators
habit: An upright clump 60 to 150 cm tall with stiff, angled, reddish stems and leafy lower half, topped by frothy flower heads

leaf.type: Compound, pinnate, with 2 to 5 pairs of large leaflets and tiny leaflets in between
leaf.leaflets: Large leaflets oval, 2 to 8 cm, pointed; tiny ones (1 to 4 mm) between each pair; end leaflet larger and palmately three- to five-lobed
leaf.margin: Doubly toothed all round each leaflet, sharp teeth
leaf.veins: Deeply pressed in above, raised beneath
leaf.surface: Dark green above, whitish-downy beneath (some plants green beneath)
leaf.stalk: Reddish, with leafy toothed stipules at the base

flower.form: Many tiny flowers in a frothy, irregular branched cluster
flower.petals: Five (sometimes six), free, rounded, creamy white
flower.centre: 20 to 40 long stamens, longer than the petals, giving a fuzzy look
flower.behind: Five small downy sepals, turned back
flower.carried: In dense irregular branched sprays at the top of the stems, side branches overtopping the centre; sweet scent
flower.size: Each flower 4 to 8 mm; clusters 10 to 20 cm

fruit: 5 to 10 small seeds (achenes) twisted together in a tight spiral, green turning brown
seedling: Two small round seed leaves, then first true leaves rounded and toothed, then three-lobed
winter: Dies right down; dead brown stems with twisted seed clusters may stand

leaf: pinnate with large toothed leaflets and tiny ones between
end leaflet bigger and three- to five-lobed
bloom: flowers massed in a frothy spray
seed: small seeds twisted into a spiral cluster
seedling: first true leaf rounded and toothed
young: leafy clump of pinnate leaves on reddish stalks
flower: pinnate leaves with tiny leaflets between big ones
seedhead: twisted brown seed clusters on dry branched heads
dormant: nothing green above ground or dead brown stems only

look_alikes: Dropwort (Filipendula vulgaris) grows on dry grassland with many small leaflets and pink-tinged buds. Elder flowers are on a woody shrub. Umbellifers have flat umbels, not irregular sprays.
